questions.prompt: Explain the library tracker's four layers by purpose. For the CLI, the models, the service and the storage class, say why each exists (and which behavior the models carry themselves), which class is the only one that touches the disk, and what goes wrong if a change bypasses the service layer.

keyPoints.text: App keeps user interaction separate from business rules and file I/O.
keyPoints.quote: to keep user interaction concerns separate from business rules and file I/O

keyPoints.text: The models give the program a stable vocabulary for what a book and a borrower are.
keyPoints.quote: to give the rest of the program a stable vocabulary

keyPoints.text: Book carries a little behavior itself: checkOut, returnBook and isOverdue.
keyPoints.quote: exposes a small amount of behavior directly on the model, such as `Book.checkOut`, `Book.returnBook`, and `Book.isOverdue`

keyPoints.text: LibraryManager centralizes rules that should not be spread across the CLI or storage code.
keyPoints.quote: to centralize rules that should not be spread across the CLI or storage code

keyPoints.text: FileStorage isolates file format and filesystem concerns from business logic.
keyPoints.quote: to isolate file format and filesystem concerns from business logic

keyPoints.text: FileStorage is the only class that reads from or writes to disk.
keyPoints.quote: `FileStorage` is the only class that reads from or writes to disk.

keyPoints.text: If a change bypasses LibraryManager, rules can silently drift or be duplicated.
keyPoints.quote: if a change bypasses `LibraryManager`, rules can silently drift or be duplicated

questions.prompt: Describe a book's checkout state as the small state machine the codebase map calls it. What may be populated for a checked-out book, what does the code expect of the checkout fields as a group and what enforces that, which flag does LibraryManager check before checkout or return, what it does not check on load, and the resulting risk.

keyPoints.text: Checked out: checkedOut is true and the borrower and date fields may be populated.
keyPoints.quote: checked-out book: `checkedOut == true`, borrower/date fields may be populated

keyPoints.text: The fields are expected to stay consistent as a group, but no explicit validator enforces every combination.
keyPoints.quote: the code expects these fields to stay consistent as a group, even though there is no explicit validator enforcing every combination

keyPoints.text: LibraryManager checks book.isCheckedOut() before allowing a return or a checkout.
keyPoints.quote: checks `book.isCheckedOut()` before allowing return or checkout

keyPoints.text: On load nothing checks that borrowerId, checkedOutAt and dueDate agree with the flag.
keyPoints.quote: it does not explicitly validate that `borrowerId`, `checkedOutAt`, and `dueDate` are consistent with that flag on load

keyPoints.text: So corrupted or hand-edited data can produce states the UI was not designed for.
keyPoints.quote: corrupted or hand-edited data could produce states the UI was not designed for

questions.prompt: Where does the library tracker read the clock, and why does the codebase map flag it? Explain where the checkout date and the overdue display get the current date, where the overdue rule itself lives and how it receives today, why date logic is brittle, and where the logic may need to move.

keyPoints.text: Checkout reads LocalDate.now() in LibraryManager and passes it to Book.checkOut.
The overdue display reads LocalDate.now() in App.
The overdue rule itself is Book.isOverdue(today): the date is a parameter, and App supplies now.
Anything date-related can be surprisingly brittle in tests and future feature work.
keyPoints.quote: anything date-related can be surprisingly brittle in tests and during future feature work

keyPoints.text: If overdue behavior matters more, the logic may need to move to the service or model layer to avoid duplication.
keyPoints.quote: if overdue behavior becomes more important, logic may need to move to the service or model layer to avoid duplication
